title: RCMP shoot, kill man armed with knife at Duncan RV park
article: In a shocking incident on Sunday evening, RCMP officers shot and killed 39-year-old Derek Welton at a Duncan campground.
Members from the North Cowichan/ Duncan detachment were responding to an abandoned 911 call when the situation deteriorated, and a senior officer fired at Welton, who later died in hospital.

Shortly after 6 p.m. on Sunday, officers responded to the abandoned emergency call from a residence in the Duncan R.V. Park, located on Boys Road. Upon arrival, the members established a dialogue with the lone occupant of the trailer. A senior officer engaged Welton in a face-to-face conversation inside the trailer in an attempt to bring the situation under control. Welton was armed with a knife, and when the situation deteriorated, officers used several force options, including the deployment of a taser, to no avail. A senior officer then shot Welton, who was rushed to the Cowichan District Hospital by ambulance. Despite receiving immediate care, he died at the hospital shortly before 8 p.m.
According to Cpl. Darren Lagan of the Island District RCMP, local officers were familiar with Welton from previous incidents, and were aware of a history of violence.
"They have dealt with him in the past," Lagan confirmed. "It's not uncommon to build a personal information bank about someone."
Campground manager Wolfgang Mader confirmed that Welton had been living at the park for "a couple of years."
"He's had a problem with the police before, but I wouldn't know what it was about," said Mader, adding that he had never had concerns about him.
The campground was locked down on Monday while the investigation proceeded.
"The park is closed up," said Mader. "Nobody can come in. The police haven't talked to me at all."
Based on previous knowledge of the residence, five officers responded to the abandoned 911 call. None were injured in the incident.
"Obviously for us it's a difficult situation to deal with," said Lagan. "The officers are doing as well as can be expected."

The incident is being investigated by the Vancouver Island Integrated Major Crime Unit, with an investigational team led by officers from the Victoria Police Department. An autopsy will be conducted by the BC Coroner's Service.

Parallel to the investigation, the RCMP is providing support to the officer involved in the shooting -- a veteran member with more than 20 years of experience -- and the other four officers who were on the scene. Welton's family is also being attended to.
"Victim Services is involved with the family, and will continue to be until they are no longer required," said Lagan.
The Duncan R.V. Park was the site of another fatal shooting less than four months ago.
Robert Anthony Harper was shot and killed Nov. 3.

Bruce Richard Voigt, 67, who was a new tenant of the park at the time, faces charges of second-degree murder. Residents and guests had to be temporarily evacuated after the incident but no one else was hurt.
